title: The Rich Young Ruler had what many people want.
paragraphs: The Rich Young Ruler had what many people want.

Wealth.
Status.
Morality.
Religious discipline.
And yet he still felt something missing.
So he ran to Jesus and asked the most important question a person can ask:

“What must I do to inherit eternal life?”
(Mark 10:17)
Jesus reminded him of the commandments.
The young man confidently replied that he had kept them since childhood.
Imagine that moment.
From the outside, his life looked impressive.
But then Scripture says something powerful:
“Jesus looked at him and loved him.”
Before the challenge came, love came first.
Then Jesus said something that exposed the real issue:
“One thing you lack…”

Not ten things.
Not many things.
Just one.
“Sell what you have, give to the poor, and follow me.”
And suddenly the conversation changed.

The man who ran toward Jesus…
walked away from Him.

Not angry.
Not mocking.
Sorrowful.
Because he had great wealth.
This story reveals a sobering truth:

You can be close to Jesus…
and still refuse to follow Him.

You can ask the right questions…
and still protect the wrong idol.
Wealth was not the real problem.
Ownership was.
His possessions did not belong to him.
They owned him.
And here is the lesson many people miss:
Jesus did not ask every person to sell everything.
But He always confronts the thing that sits on the throne of the heart.
For some people it is money.
For others it is comfort.
For others it is control, ambition, approval, or relationships.
But whatever competes with Jesus will eventually be exposed.
The Rich Young Ruler walked away with his wealth.
But the disciples who left everything behind walked into a kingdom.
One man protected what he had.
The others gained what cannot be lost.

“Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.”
(Matthew 6:21)
So the question of this story is not about money.
It is about the throne of your heart.
What is the one thing you would struggle to surrender if Jesus asked for it?
What do you think the Rich Young Ruler was thinking as he walked away from Jesus that day?
